a shorter period raises the required rate, a longer one lowers it.", "impact": "The headline requirement is conditional on a modelling choice the bundle does not solve for.", "obtainable": "unknowable", "would_change": {"if_it_said_x": "A 15-year period cutting the requirement toward the high teens softens the 'exceptional' characterisation.", "if_it_said_y": "A 5-year period pushing it far higher strengthens it."}}], "answer": "FACT [D-02 `implied`]: the model solves for stage-1 growth at 0.282629394532, status SOLVED, residual 0, against FACT [D-02 `price`]: $126.00 on 2025-06-26 and FACT [D-02 `value_per_share`]: $15.96. INFERENCE: the market price of Micron on the bundle's as_of date requires free cash flow to the firm to compound at roughly 28% a year for the full ten-year explicit period before stepping to 2.5% in perpetuity.

FACT [D-02 `band`]: the twelve-cell grid spans $10.76 (11% discount, 1.5% terminal) to $22.50 (8% discount, 3.5% terminal). INFERENCE: no combination of discount rate and terminal growth in the supplied grid reaches the price, so the disagreement is not about the cost of capital or the perpetuity assumption — it is entirely about the stage-1 growth requirement and the base it grows from.

FACT [annual history, `fcff`]: negative in FY2016 (−2,403,000,000), FY2020 (−69,209,856), FY2023 (−6,325,000,000) and FY2024 (−354,404,839) USD, positive FY2017–FY2019 and FY2021–FY2022. INFERENCE: four negative years in nine, five sign changes, and no run of four consecutive positive years — the price asks for ten consecutive positive compounding years from a record that contains no such run. FACT [declared absent inputs]: "reference_class_base_rates: the bundle is single-company; no reference-class dataset exists." INFERENCE: the company's own history is the only measurable class available, and within it the requirement is exceptional rather than typical.

FACT [10-Q MD&A]: gross margin "improved to 38% for the third quarter of 2025 from 27% for the third quarter of 2024 and improved to 38% for the first nine months of 2025 from 17% for the first nine months of 2024" — the highest of the four periods the filing discloses. FACT [10-Q MD&A]: nine-month DRAM sales rose "primarily due to a high-40% range increase in average selling prices", against FACT [10-Q Risk Factors]: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range." INFERENCE: the price move producing the current margin sits above the top of the company's own published five-year range. FACT [10-Q MD&A, sequential]: DRAM average selling prices already fell "a low-single-digit percent range" and NAND "a high-single-digit percent range" quarter-on-quarter, and FACT [10-Q Segment]: "SBU | (9) | (1)%". INFERENCE: the price variable driving the numerator has already turned sequentially in both product lines while the year-over-year figures still read strongly.

The accounting is not the objection, and I want that stated plainly because it is the part most likely to be assumed. FACT [E-04 ng.measure, status not_found]: "no non-GAAP measure is presented." FACT [10-Q Receivables]: "Trade receivables | $5,492 | $5,419" against FACT [10-Q MD&A]: nine-month revenue "increased 50%". FACT [10-Q Inventories]: "$8,727 | $8,875" against FACT [10-Q]: cost of goods sold "16,244 | 14,485". FACT [10-Q Cash Flows]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" against net income "$5,338 | $(109)". INFERENCE: receivables did not run ahead of revenue, inventory did not build against cost of sales, and the earnings improvement appears in operating cash — the mechanical tests for flattered earnings come back clean, and the objection to this price is cyclical position and required growth, not accrual quality.

The strongest case the other way, and it is a real one. FACT [D-02 `basis.formula_id`]: "fcff.ocf_plus_after_tax_interest_minus_capex_minus_sbc.v2", with capex taken at the gross tag PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment. FACT [10-Q MD&A]: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion", and FACT [10-Q Cash Flows]: "Proceeds from government incentives | 1,294 | 267". FACT [10-Q Cash Flows]: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)" — capex roughly doubled year on year. FACT [10-Q Liquidity]: Idaho fab "first DRAM wafer output projected in the second half of calendar 2027". INFERENCE: the $1.349bn base (FACT [D-02 `basis.base_fcff`]: 134,944,285,145 minor USD) is struck in a build year, on a gross-capex basis the company itself does not use, against capacity that produces no revenue inside the base period — so the base understates steady-state cash generation by an amount the bundle does not let me quantify. DATA GAP: no net-of-incentive or maintenance-capex FCFF figure is supplied, and I am not permitted to derive one.

Two corrections to the analysis chain itself, recorded because they bear on how much weight the bear case carries. FACT [J-14]: D-02's `net_debt.components` already includes the finance-lease liability under "LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations" (1,500,300,000,000 minor USD) and "DebtCurrent" (53,800,000,000 minor USD). INFERENCE: J-11's strongest reason — that lease-financed equipment flatters the valuation — is at least partly offset in the stock term and its supporting arithmetic ($1,247m described as "larger than the entire $1.35bn TTM FCFF base") is wrong in the direction that favoured the claim. FACT [J-20 `derived.basis.provenance`]: "exclusions_applied": false. INFERENCE: the normalised base of 128,727,406,636 minor USD that J-09 cites as corroborating D-02 is an unadjusted nine-year mean, so that corroboration is weaker than it reads — though it still sits close to the D-02 base, which is the point that mattered.

Where this leaves the judgement. INFERENCE (from the price requirement, the historical frequency, and the cycle evidence): the position is negative, held at moderate rather than high conviction, because the arithmetic gap is large and insensitive to the two assumptions a reader would normally attack, while the single honest weakness — a gross-capex base in a peak build year — is unquantifiable from what I have. FACT [J-16 frozen]: verdict SELL, conviction Medium. I do not revise it.

The single observation that would move me to the adjacent position, HOLD: two consecutive reported quarters after 2025-06-26 in which PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment falls below $2.5bn while GrossProfit holds at or above the $3,508m reported for the quarter ended 2025-05-29 — establishing the capital programme as discretionary growth spending rather than a charge against the base, which raises the base, lowers the implied growth requirement, and removes the arithmetic foundation of the verdict.

ASSUMPTION: I treat gross capex as the correct charge against the base because the fab programme is required to maintain bit share — FACT [10-Q]: "We expect these new fabs to be key to meeting our requirements for additional wafer capacity, in line with industry demand trends and our objective of maintaining stable bit share." A reader who treats the programme as optional growth spending should reject this assumption, and with it most of the gap."}
